test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 13 Dec 2022 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

__The man which was present__ at the meeting spoke against the chairperson.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'The man who was present'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'The man who was present' **should be used instead of** 'The man which was present'.**
 
• In the given sentence, **"which"** is incorrect because **"which"** is used **to refer to things or animals, not people.**
 
• Also,** "men" **is incorrect because the sentence refers to one man, not multiple **men**. The correct relative pronoun for a singular subject is** "who," not "whom."**
 
• Thus, as per the above explanation, we can conclude that the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***The man who was present** at the meeting spoke against the chairperson.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__***

 
• **"Who" **and **"whom" **are relative pronouns that are often confused, but they have distinct uses based on the grammatical context.
 
• **"Who" **is used in the **subjective case. **This means it's used when the pronoun acts as the **subject **of a particular clause. In other words, **"who" **is used when the pronoun is doing the action.
 
 
• **Example: **"Jane is the woman **who **baked the cookies." In this sentence, "who" is linked to the action of baking the cookies.
 
 
 
• **"Whom" **is used in the **objective case. **This means it's used when the pronoun acts as the object of a particular clause. **"Whom" **is used when some action is being done to the pronoun.
 
 
• **Example:** "Tom is the man **whom **Jane visited." In this sentence, "whom" is the object of the action "Jane visited."
